summary_paragraph: A woman with a long history of chronic abdominal pain, depression, anxiety, PTSD, and hearing loss was admitted for an acute flare of her typical mid-epigastric pain and nausea. She presented with an elevated lipase of 453 but no signs of acute obstruction or gallstones on ultrasound or MRCP. Imaging showed changes consistent with chronic pancreatitis but no acute pathology. She was managed supportively with bowel rest, IV fluids, and gradual advancement from clear liquids to a soft diet. Her pain and nausea improved, and she tolerated oral intake well by discharge. All home medications, including gabapentin, imipramine, erythromycin, and hydromorphone, were continued without change. A therapist visited during admission, which the patient found helpful. She was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with her outpatient providers.
